mainTopic: Why כהנים and לוים are exempt from פדיון הבן and פטר חמור: the משנה's קל וחומר, the debate between אביי and רבא, and רב ספרא's challenges about who is included in the exemption.
overview: The משנה taught that כהנים and לוים are exempt from פדיון הבן and פטר חמור by a קל וחומר: if they exempted the firstborns of ישראל in the מדבר, they should surely exempt their own. The גמרא objects that, according to the פסוק, people exempted people and animals exempted animals. אביי answers that the קל וחומר is about the Levites' animals. רבא rejects this from the wording of the משנה. He adds that אביי's logic would also exempt kosher firstborn animals, which another משנה says are not exempt. רבא instead explains that the לוים themselves are exempt. A פסוק that links בכור אדם to בכור בהמה טמאה extends this exemption to their donkeys. רב ספרא then challenges the idea that the exemption comes from the exchange in the מדבר, with several cases: a לוי who had no lamb, a לוי under one month old, the son of a לויה, and אהרן, who was not counted. The גמרא answers that בכורה follows the mother's womb, and that the word "הלוים" links the whole tribe together. רבי יהושע בן לוי shows that כהנים are also called לוים, so they are included.

steps.title: Did the Levites themselves exempt the animals?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה's wording. According to the פסוק, people exempted people and animals exempted animals, so the לוים themselves never exempted Israelite animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did they (the Levites) exempt them? A person exempted a person, and an animal exempted an animal, as it is written: 'Take the Levites in place of the firstborn among the children of Israel, and the animals of the Levites in place of their animals.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by attacking the משנה's קל וחומר. It points out that the לוים personally exempted only Israelite firstborn people. The animals were exempted by the Levites' animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה made it sound as if the לוים themselves exempted both the firstborn sons and the firstborn donkeys of ישראל. But the פסוק in במדבר (ג:מה) clearly sets up two separate exchanges: לוים for בכורי ישראל, and the Levites' animals for the Israelites' animals. So a קל וחומר built on 'the לוים exempted the animals' seems to rest on a false premise.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmudic discussion on the משנה
In place of / in exchange for

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the גמרא is denying that ישראל's animals were exempted in the מדבר. The question is only WHO exempted them: the לוים themselves, or the Levites' animals.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Did they (the Levites) exempt [the animals]?!
A person — a person exempted [him],
phrases.notes: Levite people exempted Israelite firstborn people.

phrases.english: an animal — an animal exempted [it],
phrases.notes: Levite animals exempted Israelite firstborn animals.

phrases.english: as it is written: 'Take the Levites'
in place of the firstborn among the children of Israel
and the animals of the Levites in place of their animals'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's discussion of the משנה's קל וחומר.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's claim that the כהנים and לוים themselves exempted Israelite firstborn animals.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק shows people exempted people and animals exempted animals. So the premise of the קל וחומר, that the לוים exempted the animals, is wrong.

steps.title: אביי reads the קל וחומר as being about the Levites' animals
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the משנה means the Levites' animals are exempt. Their animals exempted Israelite animals in the מדבר, so they should certainly exempt the Levites' own animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: This is what it means: the animals of כהנים and לוים are exempt by a קל וחומר. If the Levites' animals cancelled the status of Israelite animals in the wilderness, it is logical that they should cancel the status of their own.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge. He shifts the subject of the קל וחומר from the לוים themselves to their animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי accepts the פסוק's rule that animals exempted animals. He builds the קל וחומר on that rule: the Levites' animals had the power to cancel firstborn status for other people's animals, so they surely cancel it for animals of their own owners. This keeps the משנה's ruling, but it requires reading the משנה's words differently.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what [the משנה] means (a reinterpretation)
An a fortiori argument (from the lesser case to the greater)

phrases.english: Abaye said: This is what [the mishna] is saying:
priests and Levites — their animals are exempt
by an a fortiori argument —
if the animals of the Levites cancelled
[the status of] the animals of the Israelites in the wilderness,

phrases.aramaic: דִּין הוּא שֶׁתַּפְקִיעַ אֶת שֶׁל עַצְמָן.
phrases.english: it is logical that they should cancel [the status of] their own.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 1 by reinterpreting the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the משנה's subject (הכי קאמר)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to say the לוים themselves exempted Israelite animals.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה means the Levites' animals are exempt, because those animals exempted Israelite animals in the מדבר.

steps.title: רבא: the משנה says 'they' exempted
steps.stepSummary: רבא objects that the משנה's wording clearly refers to the כהנים and לוים themselves, not to their animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: But it teaches 'they exempted', referring to them!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks אביי's answer from the wording. The משנה says 'פטרו', meaning 'they' (the people) exempted, so it cannot be about the animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's reading made the animals the subject of the קל וחומר. But the verb in the משנה points to the כהנים and לוים themselves. רבא says אביי's reinterpretation does not fit the plain text.

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
But it teaches 'they exempted' — [meaning] them!
phrases.notes: The subject is the כהנים and לוים, not their animals.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא: וְהָא פָּטְרוּ אִינְהוּ קָתָנֵי
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's reading that the קל וחומר is about the Levites' animals.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's verb 'פטרו' has the people as its subject, so אביי's reading goes against the text.

steps.title: רבא's second objection: they would also be exempt from kosher firstborn animals
steps.stepSummary: If the Levites' animals exempt their own animals by קל וחומר, they should be exempt even from בכור בהמה טהורה. Yet another משנה says they are not exempt from that.
steps.simpleTranslation: Furthermore, if so, they should be exempt even from the firstborn of a kosher animal! Why did we learn: They were not exempted from the firstborn of a kosher animal, but only from redemption of the son and the firstborn donkey?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds a second, stronger objection to אביי. Following אביי's logic leads to a result that contradicts a different משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the מדבר, the Levites' animals exempted all Israelite firstborn animals, including kosher ones. So אביי's קל וחומר should exempt the Levites' kosher firstborn animals too. But the משנה (on 13a) rules that כהנים and לוים still have בכור בהמה טהורה, and are exempt only from פדיון הבן and פטר חמור. So אביי's reasoning proves too much.

keyTerms.meaning: Why then did we learn (in a משנה)?

steps.whatToRemember: אביי tried to save the משנה by saying the קל וחומר is about the Levites' animals. רבא rejects this twice: (1) the משנה's word 'פטרו' refers to the people, and (2) the logic would also exempt kosher firstborn animals, which contradicts the משנה that says they are not exempt.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the rule that כהנים and לוים are exempt only from פדיון הבן and פטר חמור, not from בכור בהמה טהורה. Any explanation of the קל וחומר must fit that limit.

phrases.english: And furthermore, if it is so,
they should be exempt even from the firstborn of a kosher animal!
Why [then] did we learn:
They were not exempted from the firstborn of a kosher animal,
but only from redemption of the son and the firstborn donkey?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second objection against אביי, alongside the wording objection in Step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's קל וחומר based on the Levites' animals.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The Levites' animals exempted even kosher Israelite firstborn animals in the מדבר. So אביי's קל וחומר would exempt their kosher firstborns too, which contradicts the משנה that limits the exemption to פדיון הבן and פטר חמור.

steps.title: רבא's new reading: the Levites themselves are exempt
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the משנה refers to the כהנים and לוים themselves. They are exempt by a קל וחומר from what happened in the מדבר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said this is what the משנה means: כהנים and לוים exempted themselves by a קל וחומר. If the holiness of the לוים cancelled the firstborn holiness of the Israelites in the מדבר, shouldn't it cancel their own?
steps.whatsHappening: Since אביי's reading (that the משנה means the Levites' animals) was rejected, רבא gives a different explanation of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the מדבר, the לוים took the place of the Israelite firstborns, which 'cancelled' those firstborns' holiness. רבא argues: if the Levites' holiness could cancel someone else's firstborn status, it can surely cancel firstborn status within their own families. This fits the משנה's wording, which speaks of the people themselves, so רבא's own objection in Step 3 does not apply.

keyTerms.meaning: An argument from a weaker case to a stronger one (a fortiori)

steps.whyThisMatters: This קל וחומר becomes the main basis for the Levites' exemption. רב ספרא's later challenges about a לוי under one month, a לויה, and אהרן all test this reasoning.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said,
this is what [the mishna] teaches:
Priests and Levites exempted themselves
by an a fortiori argument:
If the sanctity of the Levites cancelled
the [firstborn] sanctity of the Israelites in the wilderness,
should it not cancel their own?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces אביי's rejected reading with a new explanation of the משנה
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the משנה's subject: the people, not their animals
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה refers to the Levites' animals (אביי)
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה refers to the כהנים and לוים themselves, exempt by a קל וחומר from the מדבר exchange

steps.title: We have a source for people; what about non-kosher animals?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: the קל וחומר covers the Levites' own firstborn sons, but where do we learn that their donkeys are also exempt?
steps.simpleTranslation: We have found a source for people. For non-kosher animals, from where do we know?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices a gap in רבא's explanation and asks for a source. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's קל וחומר is about the Levites themselves as firstborn people. But the משנה is about פטר חמור (firstborn donkeys). So we still need a source that extends the exemption from people to non-kosher animals.

keyTerms.meaning: We have found (a source for one case)
A non-kosher animal, here a donkey

phrases.english: We have found [a source for] a person;
a non-kosher animal, from where do we know?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what is still missing from רבא's explanation
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that the Levites' donkeys are exempt from בכור status

steps.title: The verse links firstborn people to firstborn non-kosher animals
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק places בכור אדם next to בכור בהמה טמאה. So whoever is exempt from one is exempt from the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'Yet you shall surely redeem the firstborn of man, and the firstborn of the non-kosher animal you shall redeem.' Whoever is subject to firstborn of a person is subject to firstborn of a non-kosher animal. Whoever is not subject to firstborn of a person is not subject to firstborn of a non-kosher animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a פסוק that ties the two kinds of firstborn together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the תורה mentions redeeming a firstborn son and a firstborn non-kosher animal in one sentence, they share the same rules. The לוים are not subject to בכור אדם (by רבא's קל וחומר). So they are also not subject to בכור בהמה טמאה, and their donkeys are exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: A human firstborn (redeemed through פדיון הבן)
He is included / subject to it

steps.whatToRemember: רבא's full picture: the לוים themselves are exempt by קל וחומר, and the פסוק's link of בכור אדם to בכור בהמה טמאה extends that exemption to their donkeys.

phrases.english: The verse states:
"Yet you shall surely redeem
the firstborn of man,
and the firstborn of the non-kosher animal you shall redeem" (Numbers 18:15);
whoever is subject to [the law of] a human firstborn
is subject to [the law of] a firstborn non-kosher animal,
and whoever is not subject to a human firstborn
is not subject to a firstborn non-kosher animal.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק links בכור אדם and בכור בהמה טמאה, so the Levites' exemption as people carries over to their donkeys

steps.title: רב ספרא: what about a Levite who owned no lamb?
steps.stepSummary: רב ספרא challenges אביי. If the Levites' animals are exempt because they cancelled Israelite firstborn status, only a לוי who actually had a lamb in the מדבר should be exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ספרא said to אביי: According to you, who said the משנה means 'their animals': a לוי who had a lamb that cancelled [Israelite firstborn status] should be exempt. A לוי who had no lamb to cancel it should not be exempt!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to אביי's approach, and רב ספרא points out a problem with its logic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי based the exemption on the Levites' animals (lambs) having replaced the Israelites' firstborn donkeys in the מדבר. But then the exemption should depend on whether a particular לוי actually owned a lamb that took part in that exchange. A לוי without a lamb never cancelled anything, so the קל וחומר should not apply to him.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it be cancelled (let him be exempt)

steps.confusionAlert: This challenge targets only אביי's 'their animals' approach. The next step's challenge targets both אביי and רבא.

phrases.english: Rav Safra said to Abaye:
According to you, who said 'their animals,'
a Levite who had a lamb
that cancelled [the Israelite firstborn status], let his be cancelled;
one who did not have a lamb
that would cancel, let his not be cancelled!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב סָפְרָא לְאַבָּיֵי: לְדִידָךְ דְּאָמְרַתְּ בְּהֶמְתָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns back to אביי's approach from Step 2 with a new challenge
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's view that the Levites' animals are exempt because their animals cancelled Israelite firstborn status
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the reason is that a לוי's animal took part in the exchange, the exemption should apply only to a לוי who actually owned a lamb then

steps.title: רב ספרא: what about a Levite younger than one month?
steps.stepSummary: רב ספרא challenges both אביי and רבא. Only לוים one month or older were counted and replaced Israelite firstborns, so younger לוים should not be exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both according to you and according to רבא: a לוי one month old, who cancelled [Israelite firstborn status], should be exempt. One less than a month old, who did not cancel it, should not be exempt!
steps.whatsHappening: רב ספרא raises a second challenge that hits both approaches, since both rely on the exchange in the מדבר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the מדבר, only לוים aged one month and up were counted to replace Israelite firstborns (במדבר ג:טו). If the exemption comes from having cancelled someone else's firstborn status, it should only cover לוים who were old enough to be part of that exchange. This undermines the קל וחומר that both אביי and רבא use.

keyTerms.meaning: Both according to you and according to רבא

phrases.english: Both according to you and according to Rava,
a one-month-old who cancelled [Israelite firstborn status], let his be cancelled;
one less than a month old, who did not cancel,
let his not be cancelled!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Widens רב ספרא's challenge from אביי alone to both אביי and רבא
steps.kashyaTarget: The קל וחומר used by both אביי and רבא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The exchange in the מדבר included only לוים aged one month and up, so the exemption should not cover younger לוים who cancelled nothing

steps.title: Why is the son of a female Levite exempt?
steps.stepSummary: רב ספרא continues his challenge. Women were not counted in the מדבר, so a לויה should not lose בכורה status for her son. Yet רב אדא בר אהבה rules that her son is exempt from the five סלעים of פדיון הבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Also, a female Levite should not have her firstborn's status cancelled! So why did רב אדא בר אהבה say: a female Levite who gave birth, her son is exempt from the five סלעים?
steps.whatsHappening: רב ספרא adds another challenge to the reasoning of אביי and רבא. If only the counted לוים cancelled the firstborn status, why would the son of a לויה be exempt?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the מדבר only male לוים were counted and swapped for the Israelite firstborns. A לויה was never part of that swap. So by אביי and רבא's logic, her firstborn son should still owe פדיון הבן. But רב אדא בר אהבה says he is exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: Be cancelled / have its status removed
Five silver coins given to a כהן for פדיון הבן

steps.confusionAlert: The case is a לויה married to a ישראל. Her son is a ישראל, not a לוי. The question is only about the mother's status.

phrases.english: A female Levite should not have it cancelled!
phrases.notes: Women were not in the count that replaced the firstborns.

phrases.aramaic: אַלְּמָה אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה:
phrases.english: Why then did Rav Adda bar Ahava say:
A female Levite who gave birth —
her son is exempt from the five sela coins?

steps.triggerLanguage: לְוִיָּה לָא תַּיפְקַע? אַלְּמָה אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third challenge from רב ספרא, this time about women.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reasoning of אביי and רבא that the לוים' exemption comes from the count in the מדבר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Women were never counted, yet a ruling exempts a לויה's son. The count therefore cannot be the full reason.

steps.title: Firstborn status depends on the mother's womb
steps.stepSummary: This is not a difficulty. מר בריה דרב יוסף says in the name of רבא that the תורה made בכורה depend on פטר רחם, the opening of the womb. So the mother's status as a לויה decides.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is not difficult. It follows מר son of רב יוסף in the name of רבא, who said: "Firstborn of the womb": the תורה made it depend on the opening of the womb.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question about the לויה. Since בכורה depends on the mother, a לויה's exemption passes to her son.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words פטר רחם show that בכורה is tied to the womb, meaning the mother. The mother is a לויה, and לוים are exempt as a group. So her son is exempt even though his father is a ישראל.

keyTerms.meaning: The first to open the womb
The Torah made it depend on

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the הלכה that the son of a לויה or a בת כהן is exempt from פדיון הבן, even when the father is a ישראל.

phrases.english: This is not difficult,

phrases.aramaic: כִּדְמָר בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבָא,
phrases.english: as in the statement of Mar son of Rav Yosef in the name of Rava,
who said: "Firstborn of the womb" —
the Merciful One made it depend on the opening of the womb.
phrases.notes: The mother's status is what counts.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא לָא קַשְׁיָא, כִּדְמָר בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge about the לויה in Step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Brings a פסוק that shows בכורה depends on the mother.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only counted males lost בכורה, so a לויה's son should be obligated.
steps.terutzMaskana: בכורה follows the womb, so the mother's לויה status exempts her son.

steps.title: אהרן was not in the count either
steps.stepSummary: רב ספרא challenges again. אהרן was not included in the count of the לוים, as shown by the dots over his name in במדבר. So אהרן's firstborn status should not have been cancelled.
steps.simpleTranslation: And אהרן, who was not in that count, should not have it cancelled! As a ברייתא teaches: Why are there dots over "אהרן" in ספר במדבר? To show that he was not in that count.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ספרא raises another case of someone who was not counted: אהרן himself. He backs up his point with a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ברייתא explains that the dots over the word אהרן in במדבר ג:לט show that he was left out of the count of לוים. If the exemption comes only from being counted, אהרן should not be exempt. The same would then be true for his descendants, the כהנים.

keyTerms.meaning: Marked with dots over the letters

phrases.english: And Aaron, who was not in that count —
should not have it cancelled!
As it was taught:
Why are there dots over "Aaron"
in the Book of Numbers —
to show that he was not in that count.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַהֲרֹן שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה בְּאוֹתוֹ מִנְיָן — לָא לַיפְקַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another challenge in the same pattern as Step 9: someone who was not counted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that a לוי's exemption comes from being in the count.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: אהרן was explicitly left out of the count, yet he and his descendants are surely exempt.

steps.title: All Levites are linked together as one group
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says "הלוים", which links all לוים together. Once the group as a whole was swapped, every member of the tribe is exempt, even one who was not personally counted.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: "The Levites." All the Levites are compared to one another.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רב ספרא by showing that the exemption belongs to the whole tribe, not just to each counted person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word הלוים in במדבר ג:מה treats all לוים as one unit. So whoever was left out of the actual count, like אהרן, still shares the tribe's exemption. This same idea also covers the earlier challenge about לוים younger than one month.
steps.whatToRemember: The exemption from בכורה belongs to שבט לוי as a whole. Every לוי is exempt, even one who was not counted, such as אהרן or a baby. A לויה's son is also exempt, because בכורה follows the mother.
steps.whyThisMatters: This changes the basis of the exemption from a personal swap to a status of the whole tribe. That is what lets it apply to every later generation.

phrases.english: The verse says: "The Levites,"
all the Levites were compared to one another.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר קְרָא: ״הַלְוִיִּם״, הוּקְשׁוּ כׇּל הַלְוִיִּם זֶה לָזֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge about אהרן in Step 12, and by the same logic the challenge about young לוים in Step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A פסוק teaches that all לוים are linked as one group.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only לוים who were actually counted lost בכורה.
steps.terutzMaskana: All לוים share the exemption as one tribe, whether or not they were counted.

steps.title: How do we know כהנים are included?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a source showing that כהנים, like אהרן, are part of the group called "לוים" that replaced the בכורות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Priests — from where do we know [that they are included]?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short follow-up question. It is setting up the next step, where it will bring a source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 said the word "הלוים" includes every member of the tribe. But אהרן was a כהן, and כהנים are a special group with their own name. So we still need a source that the word "לוים" also covers כהנים.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know this? (asking for a source)

phrases.english: Priests — from where do we know?
phrases.notes: He's asking how we know the word "הלוים" includes the כהנים too, like אהרן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on the answer in step 13 by asking how that answer reaches אהרן, who was a כהן.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that כהנים are included when the תורה says "הלוים".

steps.title: כהנים are called לוים in 24 places
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי teaches that the תנ"ך calls כהנים "לוים" in 24 places. One example is "וְהַכֹּהֲנִים הַלְוִיִּם בְּנֵי צָדוֹק". So כהנים are part of the לוים, and אהרן was exempt along with them.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is like the teaching of רבי יהושע בן לוי, because רבי יהושע בן לוי said: In twenty-four places the priests are called "Levites", and this is one of them: "But the priests, the Levites, the sons of צדוק".
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by quoting רבי יהושע בן לוי. He shows that the תנ"ך often uses the word "לוים" for כהנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the תנ"ך regularly calls כהנים "לוים", the word "הלוים" in the swap with the בכורות includes כהנים too. That means אהרן was part of the group that was swapped, even though dots appear over his name in the count. This completes the answer to רב ספרא's challenge about אהרן from step 12.

keyTerms.meaning: Levites; here it is shown to include כהנים as well
The sons of צדוק, a family of כהנים (from יחזקאל)

steps.whatToRemember: The word "לוים" in the תנ"ך can include כהנים. So when the whole tribe of לוי replaced the בכורות, אהרן and the כהנים were included, and they too were exempt.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think כהנים are a separate tribe. כהנים are a family inside the tribe of לוי. That is why the תנ"ך can call them "לוים".
steps.whyThisMatters: This closes רב ספרא's challenge from step 12. It shows that the group swap covered the whole tribe, including the כהנים.

phrases.english: It is like the teaching of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi,
because Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
In twenty-four places
the priests are called "Levites",
and this is one of them:
"But the priests, the Levites, the sons of Zadok."
phrases.notes: יחזקאל מד:טו. The פסוק calls the כהנים "לוים".

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14 by bringing a source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The תנ"ך calls כהנים "לוים" in 24 places, for example "וְהַכֹּהֲנִים הַלְוִיִּם בְּנֵי צָדוֹק". So כהנים are included in "הלוים".
